feedback: Written before this candidate has raced, so it states no outcome for it. The evidence is iteration 9 (wheel_radius 0.044 m): s-bend progress 0.1604, slalom 0.110, oval 0.11, max_error 0.0617 (s-bend), 0.0676 (slalom) and 0.062 (oval), all under the 0.069 band. Iteration 8 (0.04 m) gave a smaller gain with max_error 0.0684 on the s-bend, so the s-bend margin is narrowing with each speed step. Iterations 6 and 7 showed that mass 0.5 kg and wheel_track 0.14 m both lower progress, so those stay fixed. Earlier controller gain changes (iterations 0, 1, 4) barely moved max_error, so I kept the controller unchanged to make this a clean repeatability check. Interpret the next race as follows. If progress holds at or above 0.158 on the s-bend and 0.110 on the slalom, and max_error stays at or below 0.069 on every track, keep wheel_radius 0.044 m as the final geometry. If max_error goes above 0.069 on the slalom or s-bend, return to wheel_radius 0.04 m, which is the iteration 8 best, and leave any remaining gain to the controller. If progress holds but noise_robustness is low, the unseen track may push the robot off the line, so favour the lower 0.04 m value.
requested_changes: If the next race shows s-bend progress at or above 0.158, slalom at or above 0.110 and max_error at or below 0.069 on every track, keep wheel_radius 0.044 m and hold mass 0.6 kg, wheel_track 0.12 m and the sensor layout at x = -0.03 to 0.03 m, y = 0.04 m. Iteration 9 is the evidence for this.

If max_error rises above 0.069 on the slalom or s-bend (iteration 9 was 0.0676 and 0.0617), return wheel_radius to 0.04 m, which gave max_error 0.0684 on the s-bend in iteration 8. Do not try mass 0.5 kg or wheel_track 0.14 m again, since iterations 6 and 7 lowered progress.

Do not change sensor_size or the sensor span. Iterations 0 to 4 showed that span, footprint and lead changes leave max_error essentially unchanged, so further sensor work is unlikely to help the final track.
